subject: Potential patient-data exposure: forensic snapshot & DPA coordination
messages:
From: security@medicore.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: legal@medicore.com
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Alert: potential patient-data exposure detected — immediate coordination requested

Hi Kimberly / Vanessa,

Our detection team at MediCore flagged unusual outbound transfers from a clinical records bucket between 02:40–03:10 UTC this morning. The files appear to include limited patient identifiers (name, MRN, last four SSN) and a small set of diagnostic notes — we do not yet know the full scope. We stopped the process and quarantined the affected host.

Per Section 7 of the DPA we have with Redwood, we need to:
- Confirm whether Redwood has access logs and a forensic snapshot available for the time window above.
- Understand whether any subprocessor (e.g., storage or analytics providers) could have exported these artifacts.
- Agree a short cooperation plan and an evidence transfer mechanism that preserves chain-of-custody and limits data movement across borders.

Can you confirm within 24 hours whether you can:
1) Provide an immutable forensic snapshot (or an encrypted read-only copy) for the 02:30–03:30 UTC window;
2) Preserve relevant telemetry and application logs for 90 days; and
3) Identify any subprocessors that had access to the affected bucket during that window?

I've attached a small alert export (medicore_alert_log.txt) to help with timestamps. We are standing up our legal and privacy teams but want to get the technical handoff started.

Please provide a primary technical liaison for evidence intake. If there is any contractual language we should be aware of (export approvals, cross-border constraints), flag that in your reply.

Thanks,
Alex P. (on-call)
Security Operations
MediCore Health
--
Attachment: medicore_alert_log.txt (text; 45KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: security@medicore.com
Cc: legal@medicore.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Alert: potential patient-data exposure detected — immediate coordination requested

Alex / MediCore team,

Thanks for the heads-up and for the logfile. We're opening an incident channel and will follow the DPA cooperation clauses to the letter. High-level plan from our side:

1) Triage & containment (hours): we will determine whether this was an internal misconfiguration or external exfil. We will preserve the full KV cache and scheduler logs for the 02:00–04:00 UTC window.

2) Forensic snapshot (24–48h): Ben Carter (cc'd) will act as our forensics liaison. He'll propose a narrowly scoped snapshot that preserves chain-of-custody. If an encrypted read-only S3 share is acceptable we can prepare instructions immediately.

3) Legal & compliance (24–72h): Vanessa will coordinate on cross-border transfer constraints and DPA notice timing. Please confirm any internal limits (e.g., MediCore requiring signed COCs or a vendor-specific form).

4) Subprocessor identification (48h): We will confirm whether CloudStor (our managed object store subprocessor) or any analytics partners had access.

Action items for MediCore: please confirm
- Whether you require a signed chain-of-custody form before we enable an export, and
- The list of artifacts you prioritize (full object contents vs. metadata/logs).

I've attached our incident checklist and privacy playbook excerpt to speed the handoff.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Trust Operations
Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: kim_privsec_checklist.pdf (stub)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: security@medicore.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-09T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Alert: potential patient-data exposure detected — immediate coordination requested

Alex / team —

I'm Ben (forensics lead). Quick notes based on the alert:
- We need to scope whether the export included object payloads or just metadata. If payloads were included, show us the object keys and checksum samples; that speeds validation.
- CloudStor is a likely subprocessor in the path; if MediCore confirms CloudStor involvement we will open a subprocessor request and pull access logs.
- For evidence transfer, our preferred default is an encrypted, time-limited S3 share with AES-256 and a signed chain-of-custody PDF. If that isn't workable we can provide an on-prem forensic snapshot under a limited-access escrow.

Timing proposal:
- 0–24h: preserve artifacts and agree minimal snapshot scope
- 24–48h: produce encrypted snapshot for MediCore review (pending any legal restrictions)
- 48–72h: finalize any cross-border export controls after legal review

Please confirm whether MediCore has a mandatory 72h written approval window for outbound evidence (some partners require that). Also confirm the regulatory jurisdiction — we believe affected records are EU-resident. That affects export controls.

I'm attaching a short checklist of artifacts we typically request (object list, server-side access logs, access token issuance events).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Lead Incident Forensics
Redwood Inference

From: legal@medicore.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-10T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Alert: potential patient-data exposure detected — immediate coordination requested

Kim / Ben / Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick responses and the proposed plan. A few legal constraints from our side:

1) Chain-of-custody: MediCore requires a completed chain-of-custody (COC) form before forensic downloads that contain patient identifiers. We have attached our standard template for your ingestion.

2) Export approvals: For EU-resident patient records, our policy requires either: (a) that data remain within EU control, or (b) a formal 72-hour written approval from MediCore legal for outbound transfer. Please confirm which path Redwood prefers so we can expedite internal sign-off.

3) Subprocessor transparency: Please provide the subprocessor roster (CloudStor, AnalyticsOne, and any other entity that had access to the impacted bucket) and confirm whether any subprocessors would be involved in the evidence export process.

4) Escalation contact: if there is an urgent need to expedite, please provide a phone number for on-call escalation (we will use it only for time-sensitive approvals).

We appreciate Redwood's cooperation. Once we receive the object keys/checksums and your proposed export mechanism we'll route this to our privacy operations for the 72-hour approval (if required).

Regards,
Marta S.
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
MediCore Health
--
Attachment: medicore_chain_of_custody_form.docx (template)
